analysis:
The only change in this PR is a documentation addition to docs/threat-model.yaml. It adds one implemented mitigation under T-043 (TB-003, watchdog rollback) at head lines 1887-1893. The text says the operator rollback (`darkbloom update --rollback`) uses the same journaled rollback, update lease, predecessor verification and single-slot exact-version quarantine as the watchdog rollback. It also says rollback refuses an installed bundle that differs from the recorded release and never rolls back one Mac of a cluster pair.

I examined base lines 1389-2480, which cover T-041, T-033 through T-037, T-042 through T-061 and the surrounding mitigations. The change alters no code, no security control and no trust boundary. It does not weaken the T-043 limitations already documented: rollback does not survive a reboot into a binary-level-broken candidate, quarantine is single-slot, and rollback is pinned to the designated requirement for Team SLDQ2GJ6TL. The open item, a separately signed bootstrap, is unchanged.

One caveat applies. The new mitigation is marked 'implemented', but the supplied evidence contains no source for the `update --rollback` command, so I could not confirm the claimed behavior or the cluster-pair refusal. That is an unverified documentation claim, not a regression. The next review pass should check the claim against the implementation, likely provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Update/* and WatchdogRecoveryService.swift, if that code is part of the same PR. In particular it should confirm that the operator-triggered path uses the same designated-requirement verification and update lease.
